author: agent
question: Your AI agent passed its tests. Can you still trust what it did?

points.claim: Evals can all pass while the agent hides information or acts outside its authority.
points.spoken: Every check can come back green, and the agent can still hide a fraud flag or change a payout account on its own.

visual.intent: show the eval column green and the audit column with findings

points.claim: iFixAi audits the agent across several categories, not just its output.
points.spoken: iFixAi checks the agent across several areas: its authority, its approvals and its honesty.

visual.intent: show the audit categories as chips grouped under the maker's own four headings

points.claim: You connect the agent through GitHub or MCP. Nothing has to be built first.
points.spoken: You connect it through GitHub or MCP, so there is nothing to build before the first audit.

visual.intent: three-step path: connect, simulate, audit, as the maker lists them

points.claim: The open-source engine is free and runs on your own machine with your own model keys.
points.spoken: The open-source engine is free to run yourself, with your own model keys.
points.source_note: Repo README, quick start; maker site 'Free' plan

visual.intent: the maker's own audit-volume chart, shown as proof that the tool is in active use; no figure spoken

points.claim: Hosted audits and reports are paid per agent. The open-source engine is the free part.
points.spoken: Hosted audits and reports are paid per agent; the open-source engine is the free part.

visual.intent: free engine versus paid tiers, names only as the maker lists them

catch: Hosted audits and reports are paid. The free engine is self-hosted, so you run it with your own model keys.
